questions.text: Define the following data structures and state the time complexity of their insertion and deletion operations: (i) stack, (ii) queue, (iii) circular queue, (iv) doubly linked list. State one practical application of each.

Explain the asymptotic notations Big-O, Big-Omega and Big-Theta. For each notation, state what it bounds and give one example function. Why is Big-O the notation most commonly reported for an algorithm?

Write an algorithm to insert a node at a given position in a singly linked list and another to delete a node whose value is supplied. Show the pointer updates at each step for the list 10 -> 20 -> 30 -> 40 when 25 is inserted after 20.
Convert the infix expression A + B * ( C - D ) / E ^ F into its postfix form using a stack. Show the contents of the stack and the output string after every symbol is scanned.
Explain the insertion and deletion operations of a binary search tree. Construct a BST by inserting the keys 50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80 in that order, then show the tree after deleting the key 30.

Consider a graph with vertices {A, B, C, D, E, F} and edges A-B, A-C, B-D, C-D, C-E, D-F, E-F. Show the order in which the vertices are visited by breadth-first search and by depth-first search, both starting from A. State the time complexity of each traversal for a graph stored as an adjacency list.

What is hashing? Explain the collision resolution techniques of separate chaining, linear probing and quadratic probing. Insert the keys 12, 22, 32, 42 into a hash table of size 10 using the hash function h(k) = k mod 10 with linear probing, and show the final table.

A logging service appends several thousand records per second and occasionally reads the most recent one hundred records. Compare a dynamic array and a doubly linked list as the underlying store for this workload. Recommend one, and justify your recommendation in terms of insertion cost, traversal cost and memory overhead.

outcomes.text: State the definitions, operations and complexity characteristics of the fundamental linear data structures.
Explain asymptotic notation and describe how algorithmic cost is expressed and compared.
Implement linked lists, stacks and queues to solve a stated computational problem.
Apply tree and graph traversal algorithms to a given structure and trace their execution.
Analyse and compare the efficiency of competing sorting and searching algorithms on a given input distribution.
Evaluate alternative data structure choices for a stated workload and justify the preferred option.

pastQuestions.text: Define the following data structures and state the time complexity of their insertion and deletion operations: (i) stack, (ii) queue, (iii) priority queue, (iv) singly linked list. State one practical application of each.
What is an abstract data type? Distinguish between an abstract data type and a data structure with a suitable example.
Write an algorithm to reverse a singly linked list without using any additional list. State its time and space complexity.
Explain the working of the quick sort algorithm. Sort the array 38, 27, 43, 3, 9, 82, 10 using quick sort and show the array after every partition.
What is a circular queue? Explain why a circular queue is preferred over a linear queue in a fixed-size buffer.
Convert the infix expression P * Q + ( R - S ) / T into its postfix form using a stack. Show the stack contents and the output string after each symbol is scanned.
Explain the difference between a binary tree and a binary search tree. Construct a binary search tree from the keys 45, 25, 65, 15, 35, 55, 75 and give its inorder traversal.
What is a heap? Explain the build-heap operation and show how the array 4, 10, 3, 5, 1 is converted into a max-heap.
Explain Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm. Apply it to a weighted graph of your choice with five vertices and show the distance table at each step.
Distinguish between linear search and binary search in terms of prerequisite, time complexity and suitability for linked storage.

What is hashing? Explain separate chaining, linear probing and quadratic probing as collision resolution techniques. Insert the keys 15, 25, 35, 45 into a hash table of size 10 using h(k) = k mod 10 with linear probing and show the resulting table.
Explain the AVL tree rotations LL, RR, LR and RL with a suitable example of each.
Write an algorithm for merge sort and derive its time complexity using the recurrence relation.
What is a spanning tree? Explain Kruskal's algorithm for finding a minimum spanning tree with a suitable example.
Explain the difference between a stack implemented with an array and a stack implemented with a linked list, in terms of memory usage and overflow behaviour.
